### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class), elevationSource (symbol, a top-level function), registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via createContext (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **57** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c45bddd47078b11b6ce388f3148aa66e30cd12bb` — the merge of head `a8b13e57297024c1c0592ce81ced7d1e295a8df5` into base `2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c45bddd47078b11b6ce388f3148aa66e30cd12bb && git checkout c45bddd47078b11b6ce388f3148aa66e30cd12bb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5 a8b13e57297024c1c0592ce81ced7d1e295a8df5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5 && git merge --no-ff a8b13e57297024c1c0592ce81ced7d1e295a8df5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2a728ba2acf52c13d1918c2afca7b79bf391e1f5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a8b13e57297024c1c0592ce81ced7d1e295a8df5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/security/app-automation-elevation.ts, packages/core/src/security/app-automation-elevation.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-body-identity.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-automation-identity-write-refusal.integration.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/core/src/security/operation-private-keys.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml, packages/plugins/plugin-security/CHANGELOG.md; the prose faces (content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx, .changeset/25653-app-automation-identity-write-refusal.md) read with them. No path is a remainder.

### ① Derived judgments

Read on the net diff `origin/main...origin/pr-25954` (merge base `cb0a2fcf`, two commits: the test pin `7bb83a968e` alone, then the fix `a8b13e5729`), the cited code on the head, card #25653 (body and all five comments), the PR body and the check-runs on the head.

**CI state at review time.** 21 check-runs concluded `success` (Check Changeset — the pr-automation `changeset-check` job that runs the real ADR-0087 and empty-changeset scans, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI/release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Type Check · source gates, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness, the three claim guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs, Auto Label, Check PR Size, filter), 11 `skipped` (matrix stubs and opt-in harnesses), and 17 still `in_progress`: Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, and a second Check Changeset run. So the derived test and typecheck families have NOT concluded on the head, and neither has `check:system-context-census` (it runs inside Lint · repo & tooling gates). This record judges the diff and the concluded gates; the dev's local counts (core 2763, plugin-security 4683, objectql 8718, runtime 7151 passed; census exit 0) are the dev's claim, not a gate verdict. The queue's own every-check-green condition stands apart from this verdict.

**Accept-set change — what is now refused, and by which door.** One door: the data middleware's single call `assertFlowSystemIdentityWriteAllowed(opCtx)` immediately ahead of the `isSystem` bypass (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, unchanged position; the diff there is comment-only). Its predicate moves from `isSystem AND flowRunId` to `isSystem AND (flowRunId OR mark in {hook, action})` through the new `elevationSource` helper. Refused: the six `GOVERNED_OPERATIONS` verbs (`insert`, `update`, `delete`, `transfer`, `restore`, `purge`, read from `delegated-admin-gate.ts`) on exactly `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_invitation`, `sys_member`, from a context carrying `isSystem` plus the mark. Reads of the four and writes to every other object are untouched (pinned in both test files). RIGHT, and the ruling's shape: one predicate, one module, no new error code (condition 3).

**Producers of the mark — exactly the two ruled derivations.** (a) `ScopedContext.withRunAs('system')` now returns `new ScopedContext(markAppAutomationElevation({ ...this.executionContext, isSystem: true }, 'hook'), engine)` instead of `this.sudo()`; the envelope is the same `sudo()` shape plus the mark. Both hook surfaces reach it: `wrapDeclarativeHook` (`hook-wrappers.ts:548`) installs the derived api into `ctx.api` before the handler runs, and the sandbox's `buildSandboxApiSource` takes `engineCtx.api` first, so an L2 body's `ctx.api.object(...)` is the marked api too; the engine's `buildHookApi(opCtx.context)` builds `new ScopedContext(...)` without a parse, so nothing between the derivation and the write strips it. (b) `buildActionExecutionContext(ec)` adds `'action'`; its three consumers — `buildActionApi` (through `ql.createContext`, where the new carry preserves the mark), `buildActionEngineFacade` (passes the marked context straight into `ql.insert/update/delete`), and `actionContext.executionContext` (the sandbox's last-resort facade, also through `createContext`) — all carry it, and the malformed-envelope fallback now goes through the same builder instead of a bare `{ isSystem: true }`. RIGHT (condition 2).

**`sudo()` untouched; platform system writes still admitted.** `ScopedContext.sudo()` (`engine.ts:23381`) is byte-identical to main and sets no mark; bare `{ isSystem: true }` writers (`jobExecutionContext`, seeders, better-auth sync, approval mirrors, `summary-backfill`'s `SYSTEM_CTX`) carry neither a run nor a mark and pass to the bypass unchanged. Pinned end to end: the CONTROL block inserts, updates and deletes all four objects through `engine.createContext(PLAIN).sudo()` and through a bare platform context, past the real middleware. RIGHT (condition 2's pin, condition 4's fourth pin).

**The carry across the parse is necessary and sole.** `ExecutionContextSchema` is a `z.object` of declared keys, so a symbol-keyed property does not survive `.parse` (pinned in core). On the head, `ExecutionContextSchema.parse` is called at exactly one place in objectql, runtime and plugin-security source — `ObjectQL.createContext` — and that is the one the diff wraps with `carryAppAutomationElevation`. The dev's measurement (ctx.engine refused, ctx.api not, before the carry) matches the code: the facade never parses, the api does. RIGHT. Residual: any FUTURE producer that rebuilds a context by parse or key-pick drops the mark fail-open; the dev names this in open question 1 (judged in ③).

**Forgery and leakage from app code.** The key is `Symbol.for('objectstack.core.appAutomationElevation')`. An L2 body gets no raw context and no `sudo`/`withRunAs`/`execute` on its bridge: `quickjs-runner.ts` installs only `object(name)` with the fixed READ and WRITE method lists plus the transaction leaves, and arguments cross as JSON, which cannot spell a symbol key (pinned in core). `appAutomationElevationOf` admits only the two literal values, so a forged other value reads as no mark (pinned in plugin-security) — and a forged mark only ever NARROWS, since the sole reader refuses and admits nothing. Shedding: a marked api's `sudo()`, `transaction` callback context, cascade legs (`{ ...execCtx, isSystem: true }`) and reference-check contexts all SPREAD the caller, and object spread copies own enumerable symbol keys (pinned "rides a spread"), so a write set off under a marked context stays judged as the automation's, exactly as `flowRunId` rides. The one copy that would drop a symbol, `withoutOperationPrivateKeys` (`Object.entries`), has eleven callers on the head; the two in the engine (`callerMayReadSysFile`, the field-owned `sys_file` read) issue READS of `sys_file` only, and the plugin-security callers sit below the bypass a marked system context never reaches, so no write to the four objects is re-issued under a stripped copy. `JSON.stringify` and `structuredClone` skip symbol keys, so the mark cannot land in an audit row or a stored context. RIGHT.

**Byte-identity of the flow refusal.** Composed from the diff, `SUBJECT.flow + " is refused — " + "position holdings, ... governed identity writes, " + "and " + ELEVATION.flow + " does not lift that. " + ASSIGNMENT_PRESCRIPTION.flow` reproduces PR1's string character for character, `MEMBERSHIP_PRESCRIPTION` is unchanged, and `elevationSource` answers `'flow'` whenever `flowRunId` is set regardless of a mark, so a `runAs: 'system'` hook fired inside a system flow's write is refused in the flow's words. Pinned: PR1's cases reuse the untouched `expectFlowSystemRefusal`, and the run-plus-mark case asserts through it. RIGHT (condition 4's third pin).

**Per-source prescriptions.** Hook: set `runAs: 'user'`. Action body: it has no `runAs`, so the grant moves to a `runAs: 'user'` flow, which an action of type `flow` runs as the invoking user. Memberships and invitations: the organization endpoints. Each is a real door on the head (`hook-run-as.ts` for the hook arm; the flow-door `runAs: 'user'` path for actions). RIGHT; no tracker number in runtime prose.

**The `runAs: 'user'` hook under this refusal.** `withRunAs('user')` yields `{ ...ctx, isSystem: false }`; a mark that rides in from an action-body-triggered write is then inert because the predicate requires `isSystem` (pinned "mark without isSystem"). The ordinary gates judge the user (pinned: a plain member's insert is refused with no "runs as system" wording). RIGHT (condition 4's second pin).

**Each path on each of the four objects, with code and prescription.** The integration file drives hook-body, hook-handler and action-body × four objects × insert/update/delete plus `ctx.engine` per object, reading the store back past the middleware and checking the triggering write aborted; `transfer`/`restore`/`purge` have no engine verb and are covered at the predicate in plugin-security (both marks × four × six). The pin was committed red-first (`7bb83a968e` carries only the test file). RIGHT (condition 4's first pin, condition 1's measure-first).

**Unmarked system routes that remain, by the ruling's own placement.** Read and confirmed, none a defect of this diff: (a) `ObjectRepository.execute()` (`engine.ts:23340`) elevates `{ ...this.context, isSystem: true }` — from a MARKED api the spread carries the mark, so a body composing a sibling action stays judged; from an unmarked host `ScopedContext` it runs unmarked, and the bridge exposes no `execute`, so only host code reaches it; (b) a hook with no `runAs` (`'inherit'`) fired by a platform system write inherits that unmarked system context (the dev's out-of-scope finding, see ③); (c) an in-process hook handler — host TypeScript, not a declared body — under `runAs: 'user'` or `'inherit'` can call `ctx.api.sudo()`, which the ruling says is never marked. All three are the ruling's shape (mark only at the two app-authored derivations), not gaps this PR could close under its remit.

**Public surface.** `@objectstack/core` gains `APP_AUTOMATION_ELEVATION`, `markAppAutomationElevation`, `appAutomationElevationOf`, `carryAppAutomationElevation` and the `AppAutomationElevation` type, exported through `security/index.ts` and the root barrel; `buildActionExecutionContext`'s return now carries a symbol key (two `toEqual` pins updated accordingly); `FLOW_SYSTEM_IDENTITY_WRITE_OBJECTS` keeps its name and members. Host-code action handlers dispatched by an action door are also refused, because they share the builder — a deliberate consequence the PR names, with a census of none. RIGHT.

**Docs census row.** Row 1b of `system-context.mdx` now describes the family and anchors at `#elevationSource`, where the `isSystem` read sits; no other `isSystem` read is added (`appAutomationElevationOf` reads only the symbol; the producers set, not read). The anchor resolves to a declaration in the file. RIGHT in reading; the gate that confirms it is in the in-progress job named above.

**Nothing shipped starts being refused.** On the head, every file in `packages/`, `examples/`, `apps/` that declares `runAs: 'system'` and names one of the four objects does so in prose or registries only; in the pinned HotCRM checkout, the three `runAs: 'system'` sites read `sys_user_position` (`.find`) and write none of the four. The dev's census holds.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/25653-app-automation-identity-write-refusal.md` bumps `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/core` at `patch` — exactly the four packages the diff moves outside tests and prose.
- Its `Clause-②: no (narrowing: app-authored hook and action-script writes to the four identity objects are refused at run time, as #25251 did for flows; the seat runs the contract review before the queue)` line is byte-identical to the PR body's; `Metadata-protocol: none` is on both. The arm is right: a served-set narrowing (a write once admitted is now refused), BREAKING by rule; `none` is right because nothing an author can write changes at save time in this PR — the save-time refusal and its ADR-0087 D3 semantic entry are the spec half the card routes to `domain:spec` (condition 5), so the `semantic` kind belongs to that PR, as PR1's own semantic entry (`18.flow-run-as-system-identity-assignment-write-refused.ts`) shows for flows.
- Level: by AGENTS.md the level follows the kind alone — `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships patch and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The banner is present and names the audience; the disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is in the gate's closed vocabulary and the body removes or renames no authorable key, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; the "What changes for you" paragraph is the ruling's fix, not a migration prescription, and the pr-automation `changeset-check` run that scans it concluded `success`. PR1 shipped `minor` under 18.1.0 because it carried the `semantic` kind; the difference here is the kind, not an inconsistency.
- Noted, not a fault: core's four new exports would be `minor` under generic semver; the repo's rule ties the level to the metadata kind, and that rule governs here. The face: the paths decide none, the changeset's `(narrowing)` arm decides, so the review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the narrowing face; no governed-surface path is in the file list (the queue guard concluded `success`).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report: comment 6408799371 on #25653; `status: done`, `premise_still_valid: true`.

1. **Open question (non_blocking): symbol in core vs a declared `ExecutionContext` field.** Answered: option A is right for this PR. The only reader narrows, the one parse on the path is carried and pinned, and a symbol is the one spelling no request or stored row can forge. The honest cost — a future producer that rebuilds a context by parse or key-pick drops the mark fail-open, caught only by the end-to-end pins — is real and belongs with the spec half, where option B (a server-constructed declared key beside `flowRunId`) can be weighed against "no declared surface without a puller". Carried: the PR body and the report say a pointer was left on #6017 (comment 6408782475); that comment is outside this review's inputs and is taken as the dev's claim.
2. **Fork, card condition 1: the L1 expression action body writes nothing** (no `api` reaches it). Reported on the card in the report, as condition 1 requires ("reported as a fork on this card, not fixed"). Answered; nothing further owed here.
3. **Out-of-scope finding, class a, security: a hook that declares no `runAs` inherits a platform system write's context and reaches the four objects unmarked.** Confirmed by reading (`deriveHookApi` returns the same api for `'inherit'`; `buildHookApi(opCtx.context)` wraps the triggering context as is). It is outside this PR by the ruling's placement of the mark, so it does not block. ESCALATED: "noted, not filed" with the seat as carrier is not a resting place for a security-class gap — whether an inherited elevation counts as app-authored automation is a ruling question, so the seat is to file it as its own card (mechanism only, per the disclosure line) or put it to the maintainer, before the card closes. The same card should carry the `ObjectRepository.execute()` third-caller note (finding 3) and the in-process `ctx.api.sudo()` route named in ①.
4. **Out-of-scope finding 4: host-code action handlers are refused too.** Confirmed (the door's builder is shared). Accepted: the ruled site is the action body's execution-context builder, the census found no host handler writing the four, and the PR body's Acceptance notes name it. Non-blocking disclosure gap: the changeset's audience line names "an action body (`type: 'script'`)" and not a host handler dispatched by an action door; a one-clause addition in the shipped changelog would close it, and it may ride the spec half or a follow-up.
5. **Remainder named and carried.** The PR is `Part of #25653` (the Part-of guard concluded `success`), the card stays open for the save-time refusal and its D3 semantic entry in `domain:spec`, and the changeset's `none` kind defers the semantic entry to that PR, as the card rules. Consistent.
6. **Gates not yet concluded on the head.** Build Core, Test Core 1–8, the three Type Check jobs, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Lint · repo & tooling gates (which holds `check:system-context-census`), Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, and a second Check Changeset were `in_progress` when this record was rendered. This verdict is on the diff and the concluded gates; the owning seat does not queue until every check is green, and a red in any of those families reopens this record on the same head.
7. **Dev flags honoured.** Claimed surface and the declared departures (core module, `createContext` carry, middleware comment, two pin updates) match the diff file for file; no `packages/spec/**` touched; `sudo()` unchanged; no reproduction steps on the card or PR text (the test file is the ruled pin, not a disclosure); the first ablation's no-op was declared and rerun with a build-surviving marker.
